script.text: SpaceX says it just borrowed forty billion dollars for chips. Is it really done?

On Sunday, Elon Musk said on X that SpaceX closed forty billion dollars in financing to buy graphics chips. Reuters and CNBC carried the claim. He said the chips arrive in the first half of twenty twenty-seven.

But a Monday filing is more careful. It describes a binding commitment signed October twenty-fourth with a fund managed by Apollo. Apollo's entity would buy the chips and lease them to SpaceX. The interest rate is not set yet. Pricing and closing conditions still apply.

Leases would run about five years. The final agreement is expected before the end of twenty twenty-six. SpaceX says the money supports Nvidia's next chips, called Vera Rubin. Musk also warned that smaller A.I. cloud firms may struggle to borrow.
Will the deal close as planned this year? Yes or no?

On October 25, Elon Musk said SpaceX had closed $40 billion in financing for GPUs. A SpaceX filing on October 26 is more cautious: a binding commitment with an Apollo-managed entity, which would buy the chips and lease them to SpaceX, with the interest rate not yet set and the final agreement expected before the end of 2026.

Sources: CNBC, Reuters (via Investing.com), Fox Business, Seeking Alpha / TradingView, SpaceX filing as reported (Oct 26). Financing terms are company statements; Musk's remarks are his own claims.
